subject: Proposal: Capacity acceleration & rate-tier realignment for Acme Logistics
messages:
From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@acmelogistics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmelogistics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity uplift discussion — Q2 renewal

Hey Jonas / Laura —

Quick note as we head into renewal: traffic spiked in March as we rolled out a new recommendation feature. We’re forecasting ~2x the monthly token consumption for the next 6–9 months. We’d like to discuss increasing our hosted commit and adjusting rate tiers so the soft-throttle doesn’t kick in during peak windows.

Key asks:
- Model latency SLOs at current commit vs at +2x
- Any discount/step pricing for a staged commit increase
- Operational impact (burst windows, throttles, fallback models)

PRIYA: can you confirm procurement timeline — we’d like to have terms in place before May billing.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Miles
Head of Product — Acme Logistics
E: evan.miles@acmelogistics.com
T: +1 415 555 0198
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Evan Miles <evan.miles@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift discussion — Q2 renewal

Thanks for the heads-up, Evan — and congrats on the launch. A few quick notes and options so we can align before a call: 

1) Performance at +2x commit
- For standard hosted API (current plan): we expect tail latency to stay within SLO 95th <= 350ms for typical sequence lengths if aggregate concurrency stays within the committed throughput.
- If you see sustained bursty concurrency (many concurrent short requests), we may need to enable an elevated concurrency lane or look at dedicated capacity.

2) Pricing & staged uplift
- Option A (staged monthly commit): +50% month 1, +100% month 2, with a prorated pricing step and a 6% discount on the incremental commit.
- Option B (one-time commit increase): immediate +100% with a 4% discount on the entire new commit band and a 30-day grace for overages (soft credits).

3) Operational controls
- Soft-throttle windows configurable by hour and region; automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant if the primary model is saturated (preserves availability, reduces latency guarantees).
- We can enable prefix & KV caching for recommended patterns to reduce token cost during recommendation fan-out.

I’ve attached a usage export and a draft SOW (v2) for review; looping in Karthik to lay out the mutual action plan and the DocuSign cadence.

Can we set a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning? I’m flexible 9–11am PT.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@acmelogistics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmelogistics.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift discussion — Q2 renewal

Thanks Jonas —

We like Option B from a simplicity standpoint: full commit increase. A couple of clarifications before we sign:
- Can you confirm the soft-throttle behavior during our peak (we have several 15–20 minute windows where concurrency triples)?
- What’s the expected delta in 95th latency for short chat-style requests (avg 40 tokens) once the commit is increased but concurrency spikes?
- Procurement: we need a signed SOW by Apr 20 to hit May invoices. Priya will lead the PO/contract.

Priya — adding you here for timeline.

Evan
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Evan Miles <evan.miles@acmelogistics.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity uplift discussion — Q2 renewal

Evan — great context. Below is a mutual action plan and technical notes to make Option B low-friction.

Mutual action plan (target dates):
- Today: Redwood sends final SOW + usage appendix (attached) — ACTION: Jonas
- 04/06: Joint ops call to review traffic patterns & spike windows — ACTION: Laura + Acme ops
- 04/10: Legal + Procurement review SOW; redlines due — ACTION: Acme
- 04/16: DocuSign sent for signature, PO issued — ACTION: Redwood/Acme
- 05/01: New commit takes effect (prorated billing applies) — ACTION: Billing/Finance

Pricing / tiers (Option B summary):
- New monthly committed tokens: 2x current baseline.
- Incremental discount: 4% on the total new commit band.
- Burst window: maintain existing 6-hour daily burst window; add one floating 2-hour emergency burst per week for scheduled campaigns.

Tech/ops notes:
- Soft-throttle: during sustained saturation we queue or shed non-critical requests first (e.g., batch scoring), and route time-sensitive chat requests to a prioritized lane. We also maintain an automatic fallback to a 9-bit quantized model variant for throughput spikes; this preserves availability with slightly different output characteristics — we’ll provide an eval set for you to validate quality.
- Latency estimate for chat (40 tokens): historical delta at 3x concurrency without dedicated capacity ~ +40–80ms 95th, depending on model and input length. If this is unacceptable we recommend a short Dedicated pilot (14 days) while commit ramps.

Deliverables attached: SOW_v3.pdf, usage CSV, and a short guidance doc on caching/batching. Ben will follow up on any SLA language tweaks for the 95th percentile clauses.

Ben — can you draft the DocuSign envelope with the pro-rata effective date; include the 30-day grace on overages?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Renewals Ops — Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Evan Miles <evan.miles@acmelogistics.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmelogistics.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift discussion — Q2 renewal

Perfect — thanks all. Next steps for scheduling:
- Ops call: Thu 04/06 at 10:00am PT (I’ll send calendar invite)
- Karthik to attach final SOW & Ben to send DocuSign envelope by EOD Thu
- Priya: if procurement needs additional line items (SOC2 evidence, invoice timing, or PO reference), reply to this thread and we’ll attach to the SOW.

I’ll also include a short appendix with suggested cache keys and batching knobs we’ve seen help recommendations-heavy workloads. Look forward to the sync.

—Jonas
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
